result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_common_neighbors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get nodes that are neighbors of both specified nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5177-L5253){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_common_neighbors( node_1, node_2, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the intersection of neighbor sets for two nodes, useful for finding shared connections or potential triangles in the graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : First node ID (int) or label (str). [node_2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Second node ID (int) or label (str). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs that are neighbors to both `node_1=` and `node_2=`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Both "A" and "B" connect to "C" and "D", so those two nodes make up the intersection: ::: {#c03a838a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_node("A") graph.add_node("B") graph.add_node("C") graph.add_node("D") graph.add_edge("A", "C") graph.add_edge("B", "C") graph.add_edge("A", "D") graph.add_edge("B", "D") a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") common = graph.get_common_neighbors(a_id, b_id) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in common] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['C', 'D'] ``` ::: ::: A node sharing a common neighbor with one of its own neighbors is the signature of a triangle -- this scans every neighbor of "A" for exactly that pattern: ::: {#86f99049 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="C") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="D") ) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label(label="A") triangles = [] for neighbor_id in graph.neighbors(node=a_id): for third_id in graph.get_common_neighbors(a_id, neighbor_id): triangles.append(( "A", graph.get_label_from_id(node_id=neighbor_id), graph.get_label_from_id(node_id=third_id), )) triangles ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('A', 'B', 'C'), ('A', 'C', 'B')] ``` ::: :::
